rationale: The assistant correctly identified the drive belt early and asked for the model number. But it then issued a generic burning-smell 'stop using' warning (the smell was a past, brief rubber smell from the snapped belt) and refused to guide a willing customer through a reasonable DIY belt replacement with power isolated. It also told the customer to run the dryer after the drum spun freely, which was a poor step. It gave no useful next steps, such as unplugging, checking the jockey pulley, or finding the full model number, so the customer was poorly served.
